page: Amazon Web Services c4.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor operating at 2.9 GHz across the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 36 vCPUs derived from 18 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 60.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 1.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is purely remote, as the instance features no bundled local storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 10 Gbps, and no GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark measurements place the compute and memory subsystem squarely in the middle 50% across most standard evaluations. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1,213.0 and a multi-core score of 10,598.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 30,959.1. Multi-threaded throughput is reflected in stress-ng multi-core testing at 34,011.03 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 131.55 GB/sec. Large uncached memory block operations deliver 113.49 GB/sec for reads and 48.21 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, it sustains 30.6 million Redis SET operations per second and 23.15 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The CPU instruction set includes AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2, but lacks modern AVX-512 and AMX extensions. This structural hardware limit impacts machine learning workloads. LLM text generation using a small 135M model drops into the bottom 25% at 62.63 tokens per second, while prompt processing for a 70B model ranks in the bottom 10% at 5.02 tokens per second. The lack of modern matrix acceleration and local high-speed disks represents a clear tradeoff compared to newer generations.

Given its compute-heavy ratio and balanced multi-core metrics, the c4.8xlarge is cost-effective for legacy parallel compute pipelines, CPU-bound batch processing, static web serving fleets, and compilation tasks such as Clang builds (scoring 24,395.0 in Geekbench). It is less suited for workloads requiring dense local IOPS, large RAM footprints per core, or AI inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c4.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor at 2.9 GHz. It features 36 dedicated vCPUs from 18 physical cores, paired with 60.0 GB of system memory (1.67 GB per vCPU). The instance includes 10 Gbps baseline networking, no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show solid middle-tier multi-threaded compute performance, scoring 10,598.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 30,959.1 on PassMark CPU, with 30.6 million Redis SET operations per second. However, lacking AVX-512 extensions and local disks, its throughput diminishes significantly on large LLM inference tasks. The instance serves well for batch compute jobs, Clang software compilation, web serving, and distributed caching clusters.
